title: Relay queue add --from <review> F<n> queues a finding…
what: lib/relay_queue.py:1171: MEDIUM: F1 relay queue add --from <review> F<n> queues a finding that the branch's check already marked MET, so a fixed finding becomes a new lane (principle 2, waste)
why: relay queue add --from queued a review finding that the check had already marked MET (the bin/wt template, fixed on master in c77fba2a before the item was filed); a cycle then built nothing, about 4 agent runs spent (principle 2).
failing_case: Live, 31 Oct: review-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json F1 (kind outside, templates/bin-wt:10). The fixer fixed it in
the same branch (c77fba2a); check-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json records F1 "Verdict: MET tests/test_bin_wt.py:45".
One minute later `relay queue add --from review-...json F1` queued it as the-bin-wt-template-that-relay-setup-writes-into: accepted, no
warning. A lane was built, a worker ran, and this review ran over an empty range. Expected: refused (or warned) with a line naming the
check record that gives F1 MET and the commit that fixed it.
pass_cases: 1. A review JSON with F1 outside, and a check record of the same review (its F1 sourced from that review) with F1 MET:
relay queue add --from <review.json> F1 --input why.toml -> refused, the message names the check file and "MET", no queue file written.
2. Same review, check record gives F1 NOT MET (or no check record exists): add --from queues the item as today.
3. add --from <check.json> N1 (a check's own new finding) queues as today.
4. A review JSON with F2 outside that the check marks MET while F1 is NOT MET: add --from F1 queues, add --from F2 is refused.
dropped_why: Duplicate of queue-add-from-queues-a-finding-a-check-marked-m (same defect: add --from queues a finding the check marked MET); the 30 Oct case (the bin/wt template item, fixed already in c77fba2a) is noted there.
